newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Sept 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Sept 26.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Armed followers of a Moslem political warlord on Wednesday pressed their assault on a big camp of the Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF) in Sulu as the death toll in the fighting rose to 12. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- President Ramos on Wednesday angrily denounced "leakage" of an important decision by the Subic Bay Metropolitan Authority (SBMA) to uphold Hutchison Ports Philippines as the winner of a bidding to develop the port. Ramos said the SBMA's decision was just a recommendation and that it should not have been leaked to the press before he was informed about it. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)

- Speaker Jose de Venecia, widely perceived as a presidential candidate in 1998, said on Wednesday he would oppose any amendment to the Constitution that will extend the term of President Ramos and all others banned from running for reelection in 1998. (TODAY)

- Police are looking into the possibility that politicians and a police officer are behind the series of bombings in Cotabato City in the past few weeks. Police said one of the suspects had close links with elected officials opposed to the Southern Philippines Council for Peace and Development. (TODAY)

- The Philippines' exit from the International Monetary Fund programme in June next year is subject to the passing of the Comprehensive Tax Reform Package, House speaker Jose de Venecia said on Wednesday. (THE PHILIPPINE JOURNAL)
- Allied Bank plans to sell publicly 10 percent of its stock to the public within the next three years. The bank, one of the top 10 in the country, is owned by the family of Lucio Tan. (MALAYA)

- In one of the world's largest water works privatisation projects, the board of Manila's state-owned water system will approve bidding rules on Thursday for a concession to run the city's water works. (THE PHILIPPINE JOURNAL)
